regime_context: The detector shows a broadening, not one-narrative, rotation with Silver & Royalties leading narrowly over Gold Miners, broad eligibility (9/16 themes ≥ trend-gate threshold), and the absolute-trend gate validated as a vol/tail control on this market — but the analyst's own track record shows only 31% directional accuracy, so conviction belongs low across the board. No theme shows the high durability/cohesion signature that would justify more than a tentative lean; headwinds from a crowded Base Metals and Oil & Gas complex are size-down cautions only, never fades.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Big Banks (rank 5, eligible, hurst_tag=trend, breadth 0.286) can lift participation meaningfully toward the precious-metals leaders; the watch retires if Big Banks sustains a breadth expansion above 0.5 or drops back below the trend gate — whichever comes first before the next check-by date.

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver & Royalties holds the #1 rank with broadest participation (breadth 1.0) and has passed the absolute-trend gate, so it screens as the current leadership concentration with the cleanest eligibility read; its ranking is a focus lens, not a return forecast, so the appropriate lean is a modest over-expression calibrated to the trend-gate staying-power leg rather than the momentum score.
evidence: rank=1 with score 2.11, the highest in the table
eligible=true and breadth=1.0 (every constituent participating), the widest breadth among leaders
durability_bar=0.7, above the gate threshold with hurst_tag mixed (no mean-revert signal)
crowding_z=0.94 but crowded=false, so no size-down flag on the leader itself
theses.dissent: The leader margin over Gold Miners is only 0.137 with directional=false on the rotation read, and rank-IC on this market's clean sectors is ~0 — so the 'lead' may be noise rather than durable alpha, and chasing the top name into a broad, unconcentrated tape has no validated edge.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO lags the S&P/TSX by 5% over the next 20 trading days

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners sits #2 within a margin of the leader and is also eligible with full breadth, so it is the rotation challenger within the same precious-metals complex; the lean is justified only as a paired expression alongside Silver & Royalties — the durability bar is marginally higher (0.75) than the leader's, suggesting slightly better trend coherence at the second rank.
evidence: rank=2 with score 1.973, a close challenger with margin 0.137 from the leader
eligible=true, breadth=1.0, durability_bar=0.75 (higher than the leader's 0.70)
theses.dissent: Given the analyst's 31% directional hit rate on prior calls, a second precious-metals overweight on a near-tie with the leader is essentially a double-down on one complex, and the rotation read is display-only with no validated handoff forecast.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO fails to hold its 2-week relative level versus the TSX by the check-by date

theses.subject: Rails & Industrials
theses.thesis: Rails & Industrials is ineligible (trend gate false), has near-zero breadth (0.059) and one of the lowest durability bars (0.24), placing it at the anti-leadership end of the table; the only justified call is to withhold exposure until eligibility re-asserts, consistent with the validated use of the trend gate as a shake-out filter.
evidence: eligible=false — the absolute-trend gate is not allowing entry
breadth=0.059, the second-lowest participation in the table
durability_bar=0.24, among the weakest trend-health readings
theses.dissent: The trend-gate discipline is about drawdown control, not a reliable underweight signal — an avoid lean on a deep laggard still risks missing a sharp snap-back if the theme mean-reverts strongly.

falsifier.text: The Rails & Industrials theme moves back above its trend-gate threshold (becomes eligible) within 20 trading days

check.reason: theme has no scalar etf_proxy → not cleanly scorable

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
